title: Merge a range into one clip, and break it apart again
goal: From the user on 2026-09-28: select parts of two clips on a track and collapse that stretch into one clip that plays exactly the same, the way Premiere nests a sequence and Final Cut makes a compound clip; the merged clip opens back into its parts. Split from the range selection task, which built the range itself.
notes: Split out of select-a-range-of-time-across-clips-and-tracks-a (2026-09-28). The document has no notion of a clip that holds clips: ClipPieces is one file sliced (a split adds a piece, never a clip), and a track holds separate clip layers. A merge needs a nested clip content kind (children clips on their own inner timeline, rendered and mixed as one layer), which is a PhotonzCore model change plus DocumentRenderer and audio mix work. The range is document.markedRangeMS; its menu is EditorState.rulerRangeMenuRows() in EditorState+RulerRange.swift, where the row goes. Walk base: Scripts/playtest/draw-a-range-on-the-ruler-walk.json.
acceptance: Right-click a range on the ruler: Merge into One Clip turns the covered parts of the clips on each track into one clip that plays and sounds the same
Merge is one undo step and nothing is baked: the merged clip keeps the original clips inside it
Right-click the merged clip: Break Apart puts the original clips back where they were
A merged clip takes a transition, a trim and a move like any clip
Walk at Next defaults: two clips with a cut between, draw a range across the cut, Merge into One Clip, undo, Merge again, Break Apart; photograph each step

log.note: Adversarial pass: a merged clip is modelled as a clip whose recording is a little timeline (whole covered clips on their own clock, range = window), so move/trim/split/transition reuse clip machinery and dissolves have spare. Inner clips are sealed (not group children) so ripple/lift/landing can never move them on the wrong clock. Per track merge (Premiere nests all tracks into one; the task says 'on each track', and it keeps sound on sound tracks). Break Apart heals the range-edge cuts back into the original clips. Known gaps up front: the merged clip's own sound shows no linked bar under it, and there is no canvas move of a merged clip (it has no box of its own).

Built: PhotonzCore MergedClip.swift (Layer.merged holds whole covered clips on their own clock; drawn/movieFrames/audioMix/edit-point transitions/project media/package images read through it; Break Apart heals range-edge cuts; ⇧⌘G ungroup on a merged clip breaks it apart). App: Merge into One Clip on the range menu, Break Apart on the merged clip's menu. 20 tests in MergedClipTests; walk merge-a-range-into-one-clip-walk green at Next defaults with 7 real captures and a never-blank playback through the merged clip. Left rough, not filed (no one has asked, and the audit's rough list puts them in front of the user to react to): no waveform on the merged clip's sound bar, no canvas move of a merged clip, a join transition inside a split merged clip isn't drawn, a merged clip at non-100% speed is silent, and a range-edge transition is paid from the merged clip's own spare.

Merge into One Clip on the ruler range's right click and Break Apart (also Shift-Cmd-G) on the merged clip, shipped in ba28f22d. Core: MergedClip.swift, 20 tests (plays, sounds, undo, move, trim, split, transition, break apart, save). Walk merge-a-range-into-one-clip-walk green at Next defaults with 7 real captures and never-blank playback. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-28-merge-range-into-one-clip.json.
